dependency_findings: Current first-sweep pair outputs are CPU tensors up/out. The forcing checkpoint takes both as tensor inputs; non-reentrant checkpoint retains its inputs for replay. Therefore deleting Python out/pairs references does not release all first-state storage before backward.

A single outer checkpoint could run first+forcing directly and return only differentiable force plus a no-grad per-block abs(up).max summary, avoiding up/out as checkpoint inputs or returned persistent states.

After complete global force/history, a second outer checkpoint could recompute unchanged first up and call unchanged second sweep, returning only leaf context. Its tensor inputs would be history values and eligibility rather than N-by32 first states.

Global stable-leaf history still consumes every group's force and returns every group's value. No force/value/context gradient may be detached. Both recomputed first branches share the same model parameters and immutable observation inputs; their parameter gradients sum to the original chain rule.

The finite own-state proof depends on upward only through the maximum absolute value. Its global maximum can be formed from no-grad per-block maxima; the original episode/span denominator, eligibility and finite/overflow inequality must remain exact.
Use one combined checkpoint per branch. Keeping an inner forcing checkpoint with up/out inputs could defeat the memory goal. No closure may capture up/out tensors after its invocation.
memory_limits: The up/out pair is52.57GB/48.96GiB for actual N=205369272. This is a source-supported storage size, not a measured reduction in process peak.
Additional first-state adjoint/replay storage may also shrink, but peak liveness and allocator retention are unmeasured.
The196.31GB rough nonpool delta comes from a historical global peak minus final compact-pool bytes; those times may not align. It is not a proven standalone peak.
Subtracting one pair from that rough delta still gives143.73GB/133.86GiB, above95GiB. This proposal alone does not establish fit.
The existing expanded bank, full context/VJP, global history, compact pool, layout cache, runtime and temporary buffers remain. Preparation had its own observed63.46GB peak at a different phase.
time_tradeoff: First-sweep work is recomputed separately on force and second-context branches instead of sharing one retained up tensor.

Structural forward sweeps increase from2 to3 per block. With non-reentrant replay, first-sweep forward/replay work is approximately doubled, while second-sweep work is unchanged; first-sweep gradients are propagated twice rather than once with combined adjoints.
Whole-step overhead is unmeasured. Extra site/base computation, CPU-GPU transfers and synchronization matter, even after categorical encoding/layout reuse.
An implementation would preserve equations but change floating-point accumulation order; future all49-gradient/loss/optimizer-state parity and measured peak/time checks would be required.
conclusion: Mechanically feasible exact-equation rematerialization candidate with a credible48.96GiB persistent-state target. No implementation, peak-memory fit, speed or numerical-parity claim is made. Frozen integration remains unchanged.
